steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil; coat with cooking spray.

Whisk cornmeal, paprika, thyme, salt, celery seed, onion powder, garlic powder, and black pepper together in a shallow dish. Dip catfish fillets in milk. Press into cornmeal mixture and coat liberally; place on the prepared baking sheet. Coat tops of fillets with cooking spray until wet.
Bake in the preheated oven until fillets easily flake with a fork, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven-Fried Catfish
raw_recipe.description: This recipe is a great alternative to pan-fried catfish. A combination of cornmeal and a variety of spices gives this recipe a savory kick in less than 30 minutes.
raw_recipe.name: Oven-Fried Catfish

review.reviewBody: I loved this dish and this technique. The spices used in the breading were right on, and the fish turned out delicious. The only thing that I did (since I had 2.6 lbs of catfish filets) was add an egg to the skim milk and about 1/2 cup of bread crumbs to the breading. I will keep making this recipe again and again since my husband really loves seafood (and I hate frying fish). A few words of caution, though - after the fish is finished baking, serve it immediately. I let it sit for about 40 minutes in a warm oven (husband was late coming for dinner) and the bottoms became soggy when they were perfectly crisp after just being done. Secondly, my filets were huge (4 filets equaled 2.6 lbs) and I had tons of breading and eggwash left over. Afterwards I realized that cutting the fish into smaller strips/pieces would have solved that problem by creating more surface area for the eggwash and breading and would have made smaller, even crisper pieces of fish!

I've not cooked catfish very often, but this recipe far surpasses any other I've made. I added about 1 tsp. lemon pepper, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. 15 minutes was perfect for my rather thick (1 inch) filets. I will definitely be making this again!

Cuts filets into small pieces for extra crunch. Added egg to milk to help breading stick. Added crunchy crushed potato chips to corn meal. Used Old Bay Garlic and Lemon seasoning instead of multiple seasoning to simplify steps. Made a homemade tartar sauce. Everyone liked it!

An excellent recipe. Especially for anyone who may have never tried catfish before. It will turn you into a catfish lover! I did things slightly different the second time I made this recipe. I used half cornmeal and half alll purpose flour. I added an egg to the milk. I also set the fish on a baking rack in the baking pan. That way it came out crispy on both sides. DELICIOUS recipe!
Was easy to follow recipe and loved how crispy the fish was. I placed my fish on rack after coming out of oven so that it would not get soggy.

This is simple to make and came out well. I noticed a lot of people make it frequently. My suggestion is to mix up your herbs and seasonings in a larger quantity and save them. When you're ready to make this dish, do as one person suggested and sprinkle one side of the fish with the seasonings, and then roll the whole piece in cornmeal. This avoids any wasted spices, saves time, and they can be applied lightly or heavily from a shaker instead of dipping the fish into the seasonings. You can also adjust the seasonings to your taste and repeat your successes.

Coating is just enough for 1 1/2 lbs of catfish nuggets. Make sure to dip in milk - if you don't the cornmeal coating will be too dry and won't even cook. Go easy on thyme - is strong. Make sure not to over cook fish. Pull out nuggets once they start to curl. Even husband who is not crazy about fish couldn't stop eating these! And SO MUCH more healthy than fried!!!

A tip from one of the reviewers was to cut the catfish into strips before breading. Perfect! The catfish cooked evenly. Also, I used Old Bay Seasoning in place of the pepper. My husband raved about it. We have a keeper recipe to make over and over. Thanks to the person who created it.
Big hit in my household. Batter is perfectly crisp. I added 1/2 tsp of creole seasoning for a kick

I used buttermilk as the dip before breading the catfish. I eyeballed the seasonings but most of all, I doubled the amount of cornmeal and seasonings so I had plenty to bread the catfish. The end result was delicious and much easier to clean up compared to frying catfish.

I follow this recipe all the time now. It's simple and fast. The only deviations I make is to not bother with all the herbs and spices and instead mix any of the Mrs. Dash no salt spices mixes or simply cayenne pepper with the cornmeal.
I make this dish several times a month. I use the breading on tilapia as well as catfish. We love it.

Great recipe… didn’t expect it to turn out as well as it did and for it to satisfy my craving for fried fish. While definitely not the same… it did the job well. Will for sure be putting this on my dinner menu at least a few times a month.
My husband loved it!
Easy and fast. Love this recipe. Made as written except I cooked it for 22 minutes. Next time i might even go for 25. Nice addition to my fish repertoire.
Amazing perfectly cooked will use this recipe again
used fresh celery
I just made this. I didn't have cornmeal so I used breadcrumbs and added a little cayenne pepper. I will definitely make this again. My husband loved this.

I wanted to rate as 5 stars, but I needed to stop and make more seasoning as I ran out half way through dredging. I still saved this recipe off for future use. It's very delicious and doesn't need sauce or anything extra. I served with a green salad and mac n' cheese.

This was excellent. Great blend of spices, not too salty, not overpowering and it let the flavor of the fish show through. The cornmeal gave it great texture. I thought that maybe the cooking time of 425F for 15 min. might dry out the fillets, it didn't they turned out perfectly. Absolutely will make this again.
